study: Known fixed-percentile RSC adapted to existing UWB GN CNN; mechanism screen, not novel
reused_control: shared128 ordinary24 from SWAD source; exact first-epoch replay required
validation: next cyclic source user; four train, one validation, one diagnostic only after selection
primary_selection: fixed dense tail per actual optimizer update
secondary_selection: earliest minimum validation CE including epoch0; never swap primary after observing diagnostic scores
stop_on_failed_gate: No mask-fraction/attribution/batch-selection/seed/tail/grid or full-eight expansion of this fixed hypothesis. Never swap random or best-CE to primary.
pass_next_step: Same-protocol eight-user strong controls and independent seeds before efficacy; original domain contribution must be evidenced separately.
persistence: everyepoch segment, source orders, full AdamW/scheduler/CPU RNG/best/tail, selected weights, IDs/logits/config/source hashes; epoch atomic resume; lock queue
limitations: Repeatedly researched six development users; not pristine held-out test; one seed. RSC known. No main paper fulltext obtained. No authentic Doppler/velocity interpretation. Fixed DomainBed rule differs curriculum/spatial choices in author current code; nonlinear dropout head adaptation is not exact published reproduction.
method: signed correct-class logit gradient on detached1728D features; strict less-than row2/3 quantile, batch2/3 quantile probability-drop selection; no rescale. Auxiliary head dropout skipped; final masked head ordinary dropout and CE; encoder updated only by final CE.
control: random24 computes same RSC selection in its own current state then randomizes feature coordinates while preserving per-row removed counts. Isolated CPU generator seed=base+held*100000+zero-based optimizerstep. Models diverge, so selected samples/counts need not coincide across separately trained arms.
ties: Strict quantile comparisons follow DomainBed; zero/constant gradients can mask all coordinates on selected samples; recorded and tested, no adaptive fix.
